# Gina C. Pieters, Ph.D.

> Widely published and highly cited Ph.D. economist working on digital money and assets, quantitative investment, economics, and economics education. I also speak to a wider audience on these topics, in radio, podcast, and television interviews, press quotes, and opinion pieces (from the BBC and NPR to domain-specific media). I have taught economics and finance courses from principles to the Ph.D. level at the University of Chicago, Trinity University, the University of Minnesota, and Collegio Internazionale Ca' Foscari, Venice.

The site is plain HTML; nothing on it runs a script. All pages can be read for further details; this llms.txt summarizes and highlights them.

I am Founder and Principal Economist of my consulting firm, Digital Economy Research and Consulting (https://www.digitaleconomyresearch.com/), where my work is organized by field: digital money, systematic strategy, economics, and assessment.

Contact, including job and interview requests: gcpieters@de-rc.com. I keep standard hours in Chicago (US Central Time). Pieters is pronounced "Peters."

My full CV is on the CV page, in its detailed view: https://www.ginapieters.com/cv.html#cv-detailed. The page carries the same text as the PDF, so there is no need to open the PDF.

## Pages

- [Gina C. Pieters, Ph.D.](https://www.ginapieters.com/): Economist working on digital money and financial markets. Referee, editor, and teacher of economics.
- [Research](https://www.ginapieters.com/research.html): Papers and reports by field: digital money, quantitative investment research, assessment, the economics profession, and international macroeconomics and trade.
- [Teaching](https://www.ginapieters.com/teaching.html): The courses I have taught, from principles to the Ph.D. level, with syllabi, guest lectures, mentoring and advising, and teaching evaluations.
- [Media](https://www.ginapieters.com/media.html): Radio and podcast interviews, press quotes, opinion pieces, and coverage of my research, including appearances on call-in and live television shows.
- [CV](https://www.ginapieters.com/cv.html): The CV of Gina C. Pieters, Ph.D., economist, in a short view and a detailed view, each also as a PDF: positions, research, teaching, and service.

## Education

- MA and Ph.D. Economics, University of Minnesota (Ph.D. 2012).
- B.A. Economics, Highest Honors, University of California, Santa Cruz.
- B.S. Physics, University of California, Santa Cruz.

## Career

- 2023-present: Founder and Principal Economist, Digital Economy Research and Consulting.
- 2025-present: Board Director for Monetary Policy and Executive Committee Advisor, NABE Chicago (the Chicago chapter of the National Association for Business Economics).
- 2023-present: Committee Member and Newsletter Oversight Editor, CSWEP (the American Economic Association's Committee on the Status of Women in the Economics Profession).
- 2025-2026: Lead Research Economist, Confusion Capital.
- 2022-2025: Co-chair, Emergent Money Systems Working Group, Cambridge Digital Assets Programme, Cambridge Centre for Alternative Finance (CCAF), University of Cambridge.
- 2024: Visiting Instructor, Harris School of Public Policy, University of Chicago.
- 2018-2024: Lecturer/Assistant Instructional Professor, Department of Economics, University of Chicago.
- 2018-2025: Honorary Non-Visiting Research Fellow, CCAF, University of Cambridge.
- 2018-2024: Board of Directors (three two-year terms), International Trade and Finance Association.
- 2022-2023: Associate Fellow (Pedagogy), Chicago Center for Teaching & Learning, University of Chicago.
- 2012-2018: Assistant Professor, Department of Economics, Trinity University, San Antonio, Texas.
- 2010-2012: Lead Instructor, Principles of Macroeconomics, Department of Economics, University of Minnesota.
- 2007-2012: Instructor, Department of Economics, University of Minnesota.

The details of each position are in the text of the CV page's detailed view: https://www.ginapieters.com/cv.html#cv-detailed. It carries the same text as the PDF, so there is no need to open the PDF.

## Selected courses

Topics, syllabi, and teaching evaluations for each course: https://www.ginapieters.com/teaching.html

- [Principles of Macroeconomics](https://www.ginapieters.com/teaching.html#course-principles-of-macroeconomics): Taught at the University of Chicago, Trinity University, and the University of Minnesota. Syllabus: https://www.ginapieters.com/syllabi/econ-10200.pdf
- [Principles of Microeconomics](https://www.ginapieters.com/teaching.html#course-principles-of-microeconomics): Taught at Trinity University.
- [Intermediate Microeconomics](https://www.ginapieters.com/teaching.html#course-the-elements-of-economic-analysis-i): The Elements of Economic Analysis I and II, calculus-based consumer and producer theory, at the University of Chicago. Syllabi: https://www.ginapieters.com/syllabi/econ-20000.pdf and https://www.ginapieters.com/syllabi/econ-20100.pdf
- [Intermediate Macroeconomics](https://www.ginapieters.com/teaching.html#course-the-elements-of-economic-analysis-iii): The Elements of Economic Analysis III, dynamic general equilibrium with beginning MATLAB programming, and Economic Policy Analysis, at the University of Chicago; and Intermediate Macroeconomics at the University of Minnesota. Syllabi: https://www.ginapieters.com/syllabi/econ-20200.pdf and https://www.ginapieters.com/syllabi/econ-23950.pdf
- [International Trade](https://www.ginapieters.com/teaching.html#course-international-trade): Taught at Trinity University. Syllabus: https://www.ginapieters.com/syllabi/econ-3347.pdf
- [International Monetary Systems](https://www.ginapieters.com/teaching.html#course-international-monetary-systems): Taught at the University of Chicago and Trinity University. Syllabus: https://www.ginapieters.com/syllabi/econ-17110.pdf
- [Cryptoasset Markets](https://www.ginapieters.com/teaching.html#course-cryptoasset-markets): A master's course in Financial Mathematics at the University of Chicago on the technology, markets, and players of crypto, testing where the tools of traditional finance work, or fail; students write a trading strategy as code to run on an exchange. Syllabus: https://www.ginapieters.com/syllabi/finm-31000.pdf
- [Risk and Benefits of Digitized Money and Assets](https://www.ginapieters.com/teaching.html#course-risk-and-benefits-of-digitized-money-and-assets): A Ph.D. course on the theoretical models of risk from central bank digital currencies, stablecoins, and crypto markets, at Collegio Internazionale Ca' Foscari, Venice. Syllabus: https://www.ginapieters.com/syllabi/docra.pdf

## Research works

Summaries, figures, and links for each work, by field: https://www.ginapieters.com/research.html

Digital money:

- [Cambridge Digital Mining Industry Report: Global Operations, Sentiment, and Energy Use](https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.5236060): University of Cambridge, CCAF, April 2025.
- [Blockchain Governance in the Wild](https://doi.org/10.21428/58320208.ebd76eea): Cryptoeconomic Systems, April 2024.
- [Crypto-Currencies and Crypto-Assets: An Introduction](https://doi.org/10.1057/s41302-023-00246-1): Eastern Economic Journal, April 2023.
- [Digital Currencies and Central Banks](https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-030-65117-6_6): The Palgrave Handbook of Technological Finance, September 2021.
- [Private and Hybrid Blockchains and Applications](https://doi.org/10.1108/978-1-83982-198-120211009): The Emerald Handbook of Blockchain for Business, 2021.
- [3rd Global Cryptoasset Benchmarking Study](https://www.jbs.cam.ac.uk/faculty-research/centres/alternative-finance/publications/3rd-global-cryptoasset-benchmarking-study/): University of Cambridge, CCAF, September 2020.
- [Taxing Blockchain Forks](https://stanford-jawlp.pubpub.org/pub/taxing-blockchain-forks/release/1): Stanford Journal of Blockchain Law & Policy, June 2020.
- [2nd Global Cryptoasset Benchmarking Study](https://www.jbs.cam.ac.uk/faculty-research/centres/alternative-finance/publications/2nd-global-cryptoasset-benchmark-study/): University of Cambridge, CCAF, December 2018.
- [Distributed Ledger Technology Systems: A Conceptual Framework](https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.3230013): University of Cambridge, CCAF, August 2018.
- Are Cryptocurrency Markets Price Efficient? Depends on the Data Source: Resting.
- [Financial Regulations and Price Inconsistencies across Bitcoin Markets](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.infoecopol.2017.02.002): Information Economics and Policy, June 2017.
- [The Potential Impact of Decentralized Virtual Currency on Monetary Policy](https://fedinprint.org/item/feddgm/14579): Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Globalization and Monetary Policy Institute, 2016 Annual Report, April 2017.
- [Blockchain Technology Disrupting Traditional Records Systems](https://fraser.stlouisfed.org/title/financial-insights-6462/volume-6-issue-2-611654): Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, Financial Insights, Second Quarter 2017.
- [Bitcoin Reveals Exchange Rate Manipulation and Detects Capital Controls](https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.2714921): Resting.

Quantitative investment research:

- Robust Search: Exploiting Tolerance To Optimize Trading Strategies: Working paper, in progress.
- Manufactured Premia: How Universe Construction Creates the Crypto Cross-Section: Working paper, in progress.

Assessment:

- [Designing Effective Assessments in Economics Courses: Guiding Principles](https://doi.org/10.1080/00220485.2023.2265941): The Journal of Economic Education, 2024.

The economics profession:

- Seeking Teachers: Changes in US Academic Economics Department Jobs: Resting.

International macroeconomics and trade:

- Speaking: I no longer speak at events that do not cover my travel and accommodation, and if attendees must buy tickets, I ask for an honorarium. Standard exemptions for academia and policy institutions apply.
